message.content: I’m not sure there’s a single “largest planet” that we can point to as the absolute maximum in the entire universe—our observations only cover a tiny fraction of it. However, among the planets that have been discovered so far, the biggest one we know of is the super‑Jupiter **HD 100546 b**. It has a radius of roughly ten times that of Jupiter (about 1.2 × 10⁵ km) and a mass around 20–30 Jupiter masses. That makes it larger than any planet in our own Solar System (Jupiter being the largest there). If you’re interested in other massive exoplanets, let me know!
